concept.name: White noise
concept.definition: A time series of uncorrelated random variables with zero mean and constant finite variance - a process with no linear dependence structure at any lag. White noise is the building block (shock sequence) of ARMA-type models and the benchmark against which randomness is tested.
concept.intuition: White noise is pure unpredictable static: every value is a fresh, unrelated draw, so no pattern in the past helps predict the future.
concept.mechanics: A white-noise sequence {epsilon_t} satisfies E[epsilon_t] = 0, Var(epsilon_t) = sigma^2, and Cov(epsilon_t, epsilon_{t+h}) = 0 for h != 0. Its ACF is zero at all lags (sample values fall inside the +/-1.96/sqrt(N) bands). Gaussian white noise adds independence and normality; weaker white noise allows uncorrelated but dependent increments.
concept.formula: epsilon_t ~ WN(0, sigma^2): E[epsilon_t] = 0, Var(epsilon_t) = sigma^2, Cov(epsilon_t, epsilon_{t+h}) = 0 for all h != 0.
concept.failure_modes: Uncorrelatedness rules out only linear predictability: squared white-noise-like financial returns are strongly autocorrelated (volatility clustering), so a series can be white noise yet have predictable variance. Tests for white noise can also fail to detect weak dependence in short samples.
concept.misconceptions: That white noise must be normally distributed (it need only be uncorrelated with constant variance), and that a model whose residuals look like white noise is necessarily a good forecasting model (it only means no linear structure remains).
concept.example: Residuals from a well-specified ARMA model of daily returns should behave approximately like white noise: their autocorrelation plot shows no spikes outside the confidence bands.
